title: Tommy Pham gets into social media spat with Reds’ Dane Myers over defensive metrics
content:
Cincinnati Reds center fielder Dane Myers defended himself against accusations of selfishness made by former Reds outfielder and current Philadelphia Phillies minor leaguer Tommy Pham for Myers’ missed catch that led to a 10-9 loss to the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday.

Myers dropped the final out of what would’ve been a 5-4 victory, leading to a six-run top of the ninth for the Cardinals. Pham, who has played for both the Reds and Cardinals, insinuated in a post on X that Myers was trying to catch the ball to help his defensive metrics.

After Thursday’s game, Myers said he was shading toward left field and had a discussion with left fielder TJ Friedl before the fly ball hit by the Cardinals’ JJ Wetherholt that any ball in the left-center gap was his.

Myers responded to Pham’s comment on X, noting that he is 30 and not yet eligible for arbitration, so his actions on the play were not motivated by his defensive metrics.

Myers concluded by saying that the “play still has to be made.”

Pham stood by his comments Saturday when reached by The Athletic.

“This is an issue because center fielders and infielders are now gaming the system for their WAR,” Pham wrote to The Athletic in a direct message on X. “When I talked to Tom Tango, who created this system, about it, he acknowledged it and said he will try to fix it for the future.”

This isn’t the first time Pham has sounded off on WAR and other advanced metrics. He told The Athletic in January that many metrics have flaws because they don’t take into account things like the quality of the opposing team a hitter faces or the weather a defender deals with on a given day.

Pham, 38, was with the Reds in 2022 and has played for 10 teams during his 13-year big-league career, including nine games with the New York Mets this season. He is currently with the Phillies’ Triple-A affiliate, where he is hitting .284/.418/.448 with three home runs in 38 games.
